title: Swami Vivekananda's birth chart
metaDescription: Swami Vivekananda's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 21.6° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Venus holds a square to Mars at 0.9° — close enough to weld taste to drive. A square is friction that produces motion — the aspect the tradition credits with building capability precisely by refusing to be comfortable.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 21.6° of Capricorn is the Sun's exact seat — third decan, 20°–30°, sub-ruled by Mercury in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Aquarius (4.1°), Venus in Capricorn (29.3°), Mars in Aries (28.4°): thought that travels by comparison, attraction that grows by reliability, effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Venus to Mars, a square with 0.9° of slack. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen. Behind it, Mercury trine Saturn at 1.4°, and Venus sextile Neptune at 2.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Mars opposes Jupiter while both square the Sun. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags two placements in this chart. Mars in Aries at 28.4° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Libra at 5.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 5 in air, 3 in earth, 2 in fire by element, 7 cardinal, 2 fixed, 1 mutable by modality. Air weights a chart toward language and pattern — the impulse to name a thing before deciding how to feel about it. No settled placement falls in water — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Libra for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.2° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 12.4°.
